fact_claims.verbatim: The Northwind flagship’s verified model-level thermal-incident rate was 6.4 per 100,000 installed units last year.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, or an active risk of fire must be reported within 24 hours.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The performance benchmark is a failure rate of no more than 5%. Exceeding the benchmark alone does not automatically prohibit sales; the regulator may require interim safeguards, restrict sales, or take other action based on the failure rate, incident evidence, and adequacy of corrective action.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For installed units without this capability, manufacturers must offer a retrofit or equivalent safety mitigation within 60 months of adoption, prioritizing units with known safety concerns.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Built-in fire suppression is required for new home battery systems manufactured on or after 36 months following adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a regulator-reviewed recall when a model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, calculated using verified model-level incident counts and installed-unit exposure. Regulators may require a recall or other corrective action below that threshold based on incident severity, trend, statistical uncertainty, or evidence of ongoing risk.

document.section_notes: The final S5 sets a 10-per-100,000 mandatory recall trigger, which lets Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) avoid recall, while S2 sets a 5% benchmark with no automatic sales stop, so Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%) can keep selling. The S3 retrofit deadline of 60 months is shorter than the six-year period Northwind named as a red line (NW-2), so that red line appears breached even though the document's text is within the acceptable range. Per-model results go to customers and regulators but not to the public, and the 36-month suppression timing preserves Halcyon's HC-2 minimum.
